name: Right rail / companion audit

files.note: The one trailing cluster. New `menu` slot: a screen's own Stack.Toolbar.Menu rides inside it instead of declaring a second toolbar that replaces it.
Passes `menu` through. iPad still resolves the companion to the inspector rather than a sheet.
The bug: `<ScreenHeader/>` plus its own trailing toolbar meant only the options menu survived. The menu is now a prop, so bolt and gear come back.
The ratchet. A screen rendering both a header and its own trailing toolbar now fails lint, with the reason in the message.
companion={null}: the face already lists Sessions and saved Actions, and + starts a shell.
companion={null}: the face is the three columns and a card opens the full editor.
Notes join Pinned; Search folds into the Files companion; History drops the paragraph pointing back at the screen you came from; the close button returns to every body but the commit composer.
Debounced autosave with an unmount flush, so dismissing the sheet mid-sentence still persists.
repoNotes / setRepoNotes — the same wire the desktop notes card uses.
Desktop was already right per tab; only the always-true hasQuickAccess and a mangled comment go.
The rightSuppressed branch nothing has passed true since Board kept its rail.

sections.title: The bolt was not missing — it was replaced
sections.prose:
Files rendered `<ScreenHeader title="Files" />` and then, right below it, its own `<Stack.Toolbar placement="right">` for the hidden-files menu. iOS does not merge two trailing toolbars: the later one **replaces** the earlier. So the header cluster the rest of the app shows — companion (bolt) and settings (gear) — silently vanished on the one tab whose companion holds notes.

The fix is a `menu` slot on `HeaderToolbar`: a screen hands over its `Stack.Toolbar.Menu` and the header renders it inside the single cluster, in a fixed order (actions → menu → companion → settings). The terminal session screen, which has no header at all, still owns its toolbar outright.

sections.title: A ratchet, because a comment already tried
sections.prose: The terminal screen carried a comment warning about exactly this trap, and Files regressed anyway — a comment is not a gate. `lint-escapes` now fails any mobile screen that renders both a header (`ScreenHeader` / `HeaderToolbar`) and its own trailing `Stack.Toolbar`, and says why in the failure. Proven both ways: a probe file with the old shape fails, the fixed tree passes.

sections.title: The companion earns its tap or loses it
sections.prose:
On phone the companion costs a tap, so it has to hold something the surface cannot. Audited all eight surfaces:

- **Files / Search** — pins **and notes**. Keeps the bolt; one tab, one companion (Search stopped being a paragraph about search).
- **Changes** — the commit composer, quick commands, per-file staging. Untouched.
- **History** — quick git commands; lost the sentence that pointed back at the screen you were already on.
- **Review** — Now reading: lifecycle, outline progress, comments. Keeps the bolt.
- **Board** — dropped. The face is the three columns; tapping a card opens the full editor, so the sheet could only repeat one card, worse.
- **Terminal** — dropped. The face already lists Sessions *and* the saved Actions the sheet held, and `+` starts a shell.

On iPad the companion is the SplitView inspector — a rail that is always on screen, not a tap — so Board and Terminal keep Focus and Actions there. Only the phone header button goes.

sections.title: "Pinned & notes" now has notes
sections.prose:
The mobile companion has been titled *Pinned & notes* while showing only pins. It now calls the same `repoNotes` / `setRepoNotes` procedures the desktop card uses, with the same 800 ms debounce and an unmount flush so dismissing the sheet mid-sentence still saves. Desktop keeps its TipTap WYSIWYG, phone gets a growing SwiftUI field — one markdown string in `<repo>/.porcelain/notes.md`, two editors, no mobile-only note format.

Proved end to end: typed on the simulator, landed in the playground's `.porcelain/notes.md` on this host, read back on the Search face.

sections.title: Desktop was already right
sections.prose:
Walked all seven right-rail tabs in the browser against the dev daemon: Files (pins + notes), Changes (commit), History (timeline), Review (now reading), Board (Focus — the only card editor, so it earns the rail), Terminal (saved commands), Search (recent). Nothing to remove; the rail retitles per tab instead of disappearing.

So desktop only loses dead scaffolding: `hasQuickAccess = true` guarding a conditional render, a mangled leftover comment, and the `rightSuppressed` branch in the responsive hook that no caller has passed `true` since Board kept its rail.

thesis: The right rail is the same idea on three surfaces: desktop retitles a rail per tab, iPad shows it as an always-on inspector, phone raises it as a sheet behind the bolt. The phone had drifted — Files lost the bolt entirely to a toolbar collision, its companion promised notes it never had, and Terminal and Board charged a tap for content their own screens already show. This audits all eight surfaces, fixes the collision with a lint gate behind it, gives Files its notes, and drops the companion where it only repeats the screen.
